newsitem.title: USA: Doubletree will not pursue Renaissance.
newsitem.headline: Doubletree will not pursue Renaissance.

text.p: Doubletree Corp said Monday its board has decided not to pursue its acquisition of Renaissance Hotel Group NV in light of an agreement between Renaissance and Marriott International Inc for Marriott to pay a higher price for Renaissance than Doubletree is willing to pay.
Doubletree said that, under the terms of the January 5 memorandum of understanding between it and Renaissance, Doubletree will receive a break-up fee of $15 million.
"After completing our due diligence, we continue to believe the offer we made for Renaissance is full and fair," said Richard Kelleher, president and chief executive officer of Doubletree.

"Meeting or exceeding the offer that has been made for Renaissance by Marriott International would result in dilution to Doubletree's earnings per share in the next few years, which is not an acceptable option for us," he said.
He added that, "Accquisitions remain a key component of our growth strategy, but only at a price that we believe enhances the value of Doubletree for our shareholders."
Marriott has just announced an agreement to buy Renaissance for $30 in cash a share in a transaction valued at $1.0 billion, including transaction costs and assumption of Renaissance's debt.
Doubletree had proposed to acquire Renaissance in a stock and cash deal valued at $850 million, including assumption of $70 million in debt.
